title.narrative: Strengthened skills anticipation systems and addressing skills needs for all

description.narrative: Employment data for Eswatini reveal a high unemployment rate at 33% for 2021 with the labour force participation rate at 45.9% (49.4% for men, 43% for women). Women, youth and other persons in situations of vulnerability are disproportionately affected. Moreover, the high proportion of youth not in employment, education or training (NEET) is particularly worrisome. One of the root causes for the high rate of unemployment amongst the youth pertains to low secondary school completion rates, limited access to tertiary education and Technical and Vocation Education and Training, as well as the mismatch between the skills youth are equipped with by training institutions and the demands of the labour market; the lack of adequate mechanisms to ensure young people access institutionalized career guidance services hinders their awareness of personal potential to pursue appropriate career paths. A large proportion (67.5%) of the workforce, the bulk of whom are the working poor, is in the informal sector, dominated by agriculture with more women than me in informal employment characterized by gross decent work deficits. Eswatini has been hit by environmental and climate change-induced hazards, including prolonged droughts and, consequently, to food, water, and nutrition insecurity exacerbating food insecurity and vulnerabilities of population groups in the rural areas. The strategy focuses on promoting advocacy for the development of a gender responsive National Employment Policy to address; technical and policy support towards institutionalizing skills anticipation, the measurement of skills mismatches, and career guidance opportunities for youth, as well as strengthening the policy environment for industrial and vocational training for better employment outcomes of the Eswatini’s youth.
